punchline: Thirty things to do, thirty to have and thirty to be: Canfield's list is long enough to get past the easy answers.
thirty_sec: Jack Canfield's exercise is three columns on a page. In one you write thirty things you want to do, in another thirty you want to have, and in the third thirty you want to be before you die. Ninety lines takes more than the first ideas that come to mind, and you don't judge the lines as you write. The page is just for collecting what you want, and sorting comes afterward. Canfield treats knowing what you want as the starting point.
